answer: Each identity files an opal-sealed delay ticket at the inlet queue, locking a 70-credit bond. The ticket needs 12 chained steps, each hashing the last; none runs in parallel. A whisper signal closes it; auditors replay it, and sharing burns the bond, so a rented-delay ring fails. Each step costs 5: one identity pays 60; 1,000 fakes pay 60,000 and lock 70,000 vs a 40,000 pool. An honest one pays 60 once, bond intact.
